t: You're looking at 50 Glebe Place, a large terraced house in Chelsea. It was built between 1985 and 1987 for the advertiser Frank Lowe, who commissioned it and lived here. He was later knighted for services to charity and advertising. Ed Glinert, in The London Compendium, described the house as a folly. The artist Brian Clarke made work for it. Clarke was a painter and designer known for large-scale stained glass and mosaic projects, and for working with major figures in modern and contemporary architecture.
